What the evidence can tell us.

The proposed validation sequence
01
Define the experiment

Specify a hypothesis, optical setup, sample and reference measurement.

02
Characterize the physical system

Test fabricated components and document operating conditions.

03
Evaluate measurement behavior

Investigate calibration, repeatability and sources of interference.

04
Assess the intended use

Plan any further validation required for the eventual application.

Questions that determine the next step

Which optical response is robust enough to measure? How does the result change with sample conditions? What calibration assumptions survive a physical test? Answers to these questions should define the next milestone; no completion dates are confirmed here.

Keep design evidence in context

AIFIELD’s chip-design example explains an engineering workflow. It does not establish sensing accuracy. Reviewing both evidence records helps distinguish progress in the design tools from progress toward a physical measurement system.
